title: Jumulleok Sesame-Garlic Steak Bites
shortDescription: Tender steak pieces hand-mixed with toasted sesame oil, garlic, salt, pepper, scallions, and sesame seeds, then grilled quickly.
culturalContext: Jumulleok is used for Korean grilled meat preparations that are hand-mixed with seasoning; beef versions may be minimally seasoned with sesame oil, salt, and pepper. This draft adds garlic and scallion as stated in the locked title and avoids a fixed historical claim.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 43 minutes, including minimum seasoning and rest

equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.item: well-marbled sirloin, strip steak, or ribeye

mixOrder: Combine sesame oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Add scallions and sesame seeds immediately before mixing with beef.
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 2 hours; salt can draw moisture from the small pieces and garlic can dominate.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: No serving sauce is taken from this seasoning; prepare any table dip separately.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard seasoning residue left in the raw-beef bowl; do not scrape it onto cooked meat.
substitutions: Strip steak or ribeye may replace sirloin at equal weight.
If omitting sesame, the dish requires an editorially reviewed reformulation and must not be called allergen-free.
allergenNotes: This formulation contains no soy or wheat ingredients, but labels and cross-contact still require checking.

instructions.heading: Cut and chill the steak
instructions.action: Cut chilled steak into even 3.5 cm / 1 1/2-inch pieces, trimming hard silverskin but retaining normal marbling.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are evenly thick and marbled, with no long tough membrane attached.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash hands and sanitize the board, knife, and surrounding surface after raw-beef contact.

instructions.heading: Mix by hand or spatula
instructions.action: Combine sesame oil, garlic, salt, and pepper. Add beef, scallions, and sesame seeds and massage or fold until every piece is lightly glossy.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Seasoning forms a thin sheen; there is no pool of liquid.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean food-safe glove or wash hands thoroughly immediately after hand-mixing raw beef.

instructions.heading: Rest under refrigeration
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Salt is dissolved on the surface and the pieces remain firm, not wet.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not season at room temperature or hold longer than 2 hours.

instructions.heading: Preheat the approved grill
instructions.action: Heat a clean grill to medium-high and oil lightly. Set out clean tongs and a clean platter.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Beef sizzles immediately and releases after a browned crust forms.
instructions.safetyNote: Use indoor electric equipment only when the manufacturer approves it for indoor use.

instructions.heading: Brown all sides
instructions.action: Grill in a single layer, turning to brown several sides, until the thickest piece reaches the target temperature.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The outside is browned and the center of the thickest piece reaches 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a calibrated thermometer; do not rely on springiness or color alone.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean platter and rest at least 3 minutes before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Juices remain inside the pieces when one is cut after resting.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard raw-bowl residue and keep cooked beef away from raw utensils.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Steak bites are browned on multiple sides without burned garlic.
The center of the thickest piece reaches 145°F / 63°C and rests 3 minutes.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Use strip steak, sirloin, or ribeye with similar thickness and marbling.
Sesame is structurally central to this preparation; omission requires a separately reviewed version and cannot guarantee allergen safety.
ingredientSourcing: Choose a tender, well-marbled steak suitable for fast grilling rather than pre-cut stew beef.
Use pure toasted sesame oil and check the label for cross-contact.
makeAhead: Cut the steak and mix dry aromatics separately up to 1 day ahead. Add sesame oil and salt only 15 to 30 minutes before grilling.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Reheat steak bites to 165°F / 74°C and slice for a rice bowl; use once and avoid repeated reheating.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice, ssam greens, and a separately prepared dipping sauce.
Pair with crisp vegetables to balance the rich sesame-seasoned beef.

faq.question: Is jumulleok the same as bulgogi?
faq.answer: No. Bulgogi is generally thinly sliced and marinated; this jumulleok preparation uses thicker steak pieces and a short, minimal sesame-oil seasoning.

faq.question: Can I use stew beef?
faq.answer: It is not recommended for this fast method because common stew cuts need longer cooking to become tender.
